triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a mere identifier rename or a scope generalization, and it does not hold: the pre-fix §122 exemption was gated on `entry_is_line_a`/`entry_is_line_b`, and the same diff shows those exact flags simultaneously carrying §301 list-1/2/3 membership (`entry_is_line_a and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate` → `entry_is_china_301_list123`) and §232-aluminum membership (`elif entry_is_line_b:` → `elif entry_is_section_232_aluminum:`), so a §301-listed line was zeroed out of the 10% surcharge for every origin — a condition with no basis in the §122 source. The rule's own proof atoms (unchanged by this commit) ground the exemption only on "subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04", which is exactly what the new predicates `entry_is_section_122_exempt` / `entry_is_section_232_covered` name, so the fix re-grounds a branch that was grounded on the wrong provision (§301 list membership). It is not mechanical: one old input slot splits into several distinct populations, runtime values change (the PR's witness-slice gate enumerates 18 cells "where the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part"), and the companion-test input slots changed. untraceable_branch fits better than unrepresented_clause or wrong_entity_or_scope because the exemption clause was already present and the rule's entity/population is unchanged; what was wrong was the branch predicate's grounding.

triage.verifier_notes:
Quote: the two fragments "if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0" and "if entry_is_section_122_exempt or entry_is_section_232_covered: 0" are verbatim substrings of the removed/added lines at diff lines 23-24 of 098.diff (rules[section_122_component_rate].versions[1].formula, effective_from 2026-02-24 / effective_to 2026-07-23, confirmed by windowing the pre file at scratchpad/pre98.yaml lines 2532-2581); only the leading 49-parenthesis run is elided, so I did not retype it and risk a miscount.

Corroboration, not paraphrase: the module's §122 proof atoms are byte-identical pre and post, and already cite the two real exceptions (9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list, with excerpt "7202.11.10", and the 9903.82.02/.04 aluminum-steel-copper coverage). So the citations were right and the encoded condition did not match them — the textbook untraceable/misgrounded-branch shape.

One imprecision in the first reader's reading worth flagging: it says the surcharge was suppressed on "all §301-listed lines". Per the diff, line_a = §301 lists 1/2/3 and line_b = the 2024 action (also the §232-aluminum flag); list 4A lines rode `entry_is_line_c` and were NOT suppressed. So the suppression covered §301 list-1/2/3 and 2024-action/aluminum lines, not literally every §301 line. This narrows the blast radius but does not change the defect or its kind.

Scope caveat for the reviewer: this same module diff also contains changes that are NOT defect corrections and should not be double-counted if other rule paths from this commit are scored — the new `ch99b_s232_steel_heading_rate` parameter and `section_232_steel_component_rate` rule wired into `schedule_statutory_stack` are new coverage the module never claimed (the PR says the witness's ferroalloy exemplar "sits outside note 16(c), which is why no witness slot existed"), and the `section_232_steel_component_rate` block nests `metadata.proof.proof.atoms` (double `proof:`) — a structural wart the PR's issue comment says was later repaired ("steel atoms unwrapped to canonical `metadata.proof.atoms`"). The brazil_section_301_component_rate and forced_labor_section_301_component_rate hunks are the same exemplar-coupling class as §122 (each drops an `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0` gate and adds membership gating), so they are plausibly the same kind, but both those rules' windows begin 2026-07-22/07-24 and the PR notes both actions are outside the evaluated April-June window, so their defect had no evaluated incidence.

Also note the per-module summary text asserts "This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values." That sentence is generator boilerplate about the parenthesization/chapter-prefixing step only; it is contradicted by the formula tokens changed in the same diff and must not be read as evidence the change is mechanical.
